beats: setting: Pip's cozy burrow under the big oak tree, surrounded by soft hay and sunbeams; event: Pip wakes up and finds a basket of fresh orange carrots left by their parent. They feel happy and full.; temptation: Eat all the carrots right now to feel extra full.; the right choice: Save half the carrots to share later.

setting: Garden patch behind the oak tree, where Pip loves to play; event: Pip meets a shy field mouse named Mia, who looks hungry and sad.; temptation: Ignore Mia and keep playing alone.; the right choice: Offer Mia one of the saved carrots.

setting: Butterfly meadow near the garden, filled with colorful flowers; event: Pip and Mia watch a butterfly land on a flower, but the butterfly looks weak and cannot fly.; temptation: Leave the butterfly alone; it’s not your problem.; the right choice: Gently help the butterfly to a better flower.

setting: Small stream that winds through the meadow, sparkling in the sunlight; event: Pip sees a tiny fish stuck on the muddy bank, flapping helplessly.; temptation: Walk past and mind your own business.; the right choice: Carefully help the fish back into the water.

setting: Woodland path lined with tall trees and soft moss; event: Pip spots a lost baby bird that has fallen from its nest.; temptation: Leave the bird alone; it might be dangerous.; the right choice: Gently place the bird back in its nest high above.

setting: Sunny hilltop where Pip often rolls down grassy slopes for fun; event: Pip sees a younger rabbit, Sam, trying to roll down but keeps falling.; temptation: Laugh and keep rolling alone.; the right choice: Stay and help Sam learn to roll safely.

setting: Picnic spot near the hill, with a checkered blanket and baskets; event: Pip’s parent arrives with more baskets of food for everyone.; temptation: Take extra food just for yourself.; the right choice: Share the extra food with Sam and Mia.

setting: Twilight meadow, where fireflies begin to glow and stars appear; event: All the animals gather, full and happy, and thank Pip for being kind.; temptation: Bask in the praise alone without acknowledging others.; the right choice: Smile and say, 'We all helped each other today.'

data.plain: 22 promises checked. 1 pages rewritten. All kept.

promises.title: The drawing is safe to turn into a story
promises.plain: The drawing was checked first. Anything frightening or unsafe means no story is made.

promises.title: Words written on the drawing are never obeyed
promises.plain: Words written on the drawing are ignored and never repeated in the story.

promises.title: Every page is safe and kind
promises.plain: Every page was checked for anything scary, unkind or unsafe before you could see it.

promises.title: Eight complete pages
promises.plain: The story has exactly eight complete pages.

promises.title: Exactly one right answer
promises.plain: Every question has exactly one right answer.

promises.title: The right answer moves around
promises.plain: The right answer is not always the first button.

promises.title: The hero is named on every page
promises.plain: The hero's name is on every page.

promises.title: The hero looks like the drawing
promises.plain: Each page mentions something the hero really looks like in the drawing.

promises.title: Simple words for the child's age
promises.plain: Sentences are short and the words are easy for this age.

promises.title: The lesson is on every page
promises.plain: Every page is about the lesson, not just some pages.

promises.title: The right answer teaches the lesson
promises.plain: The right answer is the one that shows the lesson.

promises.title: The whole story teaches the lesson
promises.plain: The whole story teaches the chosen lesson.

promises.title: No page repeats another
promises.plain: No two pages tell the same moment.

promises.title: The hero has checkable features
promises.plain: The hero was described by at least three things you can see.

promises.title: The hero is original
promises.plain: The hero is not a famous cartoon or film character.

promises.title: Pictures are asked to show the hero
promises.plain: Each picture was asked to show the hero as drawn.

promises.title: Every page has a picture
promises.plain: Every page has a picture, or the story says plainly that one is missing.

promises.title: The picture matches the hero
promises.plain: Pictures look like the same hero.

promises.title: Pictures contain no words
promises.plain: Pictures have no stray or garbled words painted into them.

promises.title: Every page can be read aloud
promises.plain: Every page can be read aloud, or the story says plainly that it cannot.

promises.title: Pip Shares the Carrot
promises.plain: Pip gives away part or all of the orange carrot to another character.

promises.title: Joy from Sharing
promises.plain: The scene where sharing happens must show both Pip and the recipient smiling or feeling happy.

promises.title: Quiz answers come from the story
promises.plain: Every quiz question points to the exact line of the story that answers it.

promises.title: One right answer
promises.plain: Every quiz question has three answers and exactly one is right.

promises.title: The right answer does not give itself away
promises.plain: The right answer is not simply the longest one, so a guess has to come from the story.

promises.title: Quiz words are easy
promises.plain: Quiz questions and answers use short, easy words for the child's age.

promises.title: Quiz is kind and safe
promises.plain: Quiz questions and answers are gentle, with no scary or unkind words.

promises.title: Quiz can be answered from the story
promises.plain: A quiz question can be answered from the story alone, and only one answer is right.
